Subject: SIGv2: subprocessor inventory and mitigations - HealthBridge request

Hi Diego,

We're kicking off our third-party security validation for a potential platform integration with HealthBridge. Attached is the initial SIGv2 packet and a short questionnaire focused on subprocessors and supply-chain controls. Can you provide: 1) a current subprocessor inventory with roles and data access scope; 2) any SOC 2 or ISO evidence covering those subprocessors; and 3) a brief description of your supplier risk management / vetting process (questionnaire item 5.2 and 7.1).

We're on a tight timeline for our procurement committee — ideally by end of day Friday. If you have a single CSV export of your subprocessor list that includes region and a contact for each, that would be perfect.

Thanks,
Julia Santos
Security Manager, Vendor Risk
HealthBridge Inc.

Thanks Julia — looping in Mina (security) and Marcus (legal) to own the evidence pack. We'll aim to get you the CSV and SOC 2 link by Friday. A couple quick clarifying Qs so we prioritize correctly:

- Do you need agent-level SSH keys or IAM roles in the CSV, or just company/service and region?
- Is the SIGv2 portal going to request encrypted-at-rest attestations per-subprocessor, or is a vendor-level encryption statement acceptable?

Mina/Marcus — can you take point on producing: the subprocessor CSV, an anonymized access-scope column, a copy of our most recent SOC 2 Type II, and the supply-chain policy excerpt? Marcus, please flag any contractual notes we should call out.

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Julia Santos <security@healthbridge.com>, diego_fernandez@redwood.com

Date: 2026-03-11T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIGv2: subprocessor inventory and mitigations - HealthBridge request

Hi Julia — thanks for the packet and timeline. Attached are the items you requested: the subprocessor inventory CSV (redwood_subprocessors_2026-03.csv), our SOC 2 Type II report (SOC2_Type2_2025.pdf), and a copy of the supply chain & third-party risk policy (supply_chain_policy_v3.1.pdf). Below is a short mapping to the SIGv2 sections you referenced.

Summary answers:
- Subprocessor inventory: attached CSV includes company name, service provided, data scope (minimal/derived/full), region (US/EU/APAC), and a support contact. We’ve redacted personnel-level credentials per our privacy practice.
- Evidence: SOC 2 report covers our core platform and includes vendor management controls; where subprocessors are in-scope we call those out in Section 3. Note that SOC 2 does not include full third-party SOC attachments; for specific vendors we can provide attestations or contracts on a case-by-case basis.
- Supply-chain vetting: we maintain a supplier onboarding checklist (risk profile, security questionnaire, contract terms requiring SOC 2 or equivalent, encryption requirements, and right-to-audit for higher-risk services). High-risk subprocessors undergo annual penetration tests and quarterly access reviews.
- Encryption: All customer data in transit is TLS 1.2+; at-rest encryption is AES-256 with KMS-managed keys. For dedicated/private deployments we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations.

Key subprocessors (excerpt):
- Cloud provider: NebulaCloud (compute & storage) — role: compute/storage; region: US, EU; data scope: full platform.
- Vector DB: VectorVault Inc. — role: embeddings storage (encrypted) and indexing; region: US; data scope: derived embeddings; encryption-at-rest guaranteed.
- Monitoring & logs: LogStream Ltd. — role: observability pipeline; region: US; data scope: operational telemetry (no plaintext PII); logs are redacted before export.
- Billing & payments: FusePay — role: invoicing/charges; region: US; data scope: billing metadata only.

We can provide per-vendor attestations for NebulaCloud and VectorVault upon request.

Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_2026-03.csv, SOC2_Type2_2025.pdf, supply_chain_policy_v3.1.pdf

Happy to hop on a 20-minute call if you want to walk the CSV together.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
From: Julia Santos <security@healthbridge.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, diego_fernandez@redwood.com

Subject: Re: SIGv2: subprocessor inventory and mitigations - HealthBridge request

Mina — thank you, this is very helpful and on schedule. A few follow-ups from our assessor (cc'd):

1) Data residency: can you confirm whether embeddings stored by VectorVault can be restricted to EU-only regions for EU customers? Our procurement requires region-specific controls for EU patient data.

2) Key management: for private deployments with customer-managed keys, can you provide a brief note on KMS supported providers and whether backups are encrypted with the same CMK?

3) Log retention: what is the default retention period for operational logs and can that be shortened for specific customers?

If you can reply by end of day Thursday we'll be able to close the SIGv2 track and proceed to contracting.

Thanks,
Julia
From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: Julia Santos <security@healthbridge.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-12T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIGv2: subprocessor inventory and mitigations - HealthBridge request

Hi Julia — quick answers below from our security team:  

- Embeddings residency: Yes — for EU customers we can configure VectorVault to store embeddings in EU-only regions. This is supported for Dedicated and Private deployments; for Hosted API customers we offer an EU-only tenant option for production workloads. (We will include an appendix to the CSV indicating available region constraints per vendor.)

- KMS / backups: Supported KMS providers: AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault, and on-prem HSM integrations. Backups (snapshots) are encrypted with the same CMK when customer-managed keys are in use; that is documented in our supply_chain_policy_v3.1.pdf (see section 4.2).

- Log retention: Default operational log retention is 90 days. For specific customers we can shorten retention down to 30 days (or longer upon request) via contract. We also offer redaction/PII-scrubbing pre-export for sensitive customers.

Next steps: Mina will provide the CSV with the region-constraints appendix by EOD March 13 and Marcus will prepare a short contract addendum for data residency language. Let us know if you'd like a 15-minute call tomorrow to confirm.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

Diego
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
